#4393. 10 Soulslikes Where You’re Actually the Villain

Shane is a Contributor for DualShockers writing guides and other materials. He has a degree in Game Design and Criticism.

​Of all the genres in gaming, there isn’t one that stays as morally ambiguous as soulslikes. While the genre has grown to encompass a lot of different kinds of games, that question of morality remains the same.

Players are often a bit hesitant to become the villain of the story, but offering up that potential makes for a more difficult choice. Whether a player will embrace evil or remain on the path of good always makes for a good time.

This list consists of games that could be categorized as soulslike even if their main genre is a bit different. It does contain spoilers for certain endings, so you may want to read carefully to avoid anything you’d rather not know.

If you're ready to root for the bad guy, then check out this list of shooters where you're actually the villain!

Hellpoint is an interesting soulslike game that sees players take on the role of a Spawn as they face off against all kinds of cosmic horrors. While trapped on a space station, players will make their way through boss encounters while making choices to determine their alignment.

You don’t have to play as the villain in Hellpoint, but you do have the option to align yourself with the Prodigal Spawn and perform a dark ritual. It is morally grey, but those choices do matter and can make players into the villain of their story.

In a genre that typically sticks to being morally grey, Death’s Gambit: Afterlife makes things a bit harder by making you an agent of death. In this Metroidvania soulslike, players will go up against immortals as they attempt to snuff out immortality altogether.

This one is tough because your motivations aren’t necessarily evil, but the results you achieve certainly make you a bit of a villain. By destroying immortality, you’ll be killing anything and everything connected to it, regardless of alignment.

You wouldn't typically imagine a game about giant robots digging so deep into the ambiguity of who a mercenary decides to fight for, but Armored Core VI does just that. The game is more of an action game than a soulslike, but with FromSoftware at the wheel, it still feels like one.

Playing as C4-621, you have a choice in who you help, and depending on your choice, a lot of things can happen. Despite the choice of endings, you do spend a lot of time fighting and killing the residents of Rubicon 3.

If you're tired of being the good guy, then check out this list of JRPGs where you play as the anti-hero!

FromSoftware really enjoys giving players a choice in how they affect the world as a whole, and most of the time it's not for the better. Playing as an Ashen One, players will have to face off against the mighty Lords of Cinder and decide the fate of the world.

There is still that freedom of choice, but players can choose to simply burn the world themselves. This certainly makes you a villain to some, but it is still a choice, so it’s up to players if they become a villain.

As a Hunter in Bloodborne, your only purpose is to kill the monsters that plague the world and use their power to make yourself stronger. You may not start very villainous, but in the end you may become the very thing you set out to destroy.

In one of the endings, players can turn into a Great One, an otherworldly eldritch being that doesn’t follow our sense of morality. It could be up for debate whether this makes players the true villain, but it does seem a bit villainous to leave behind your humanity.

Elden Ring was a sensational game that expanded the soulslike genre into the open-world genre and gave players more freedom than ever before. With that freedom came plenty of choice, and those choices could end in disaster.

By taking the Frenzied Flame, players will cause a chain reaction of events that ends the game with the world on fire. The world may be a bit problematic, but causing mass destruction and burning the world to a crisp seems very villainous.

While playing as the protagonist, Wolf, players are given choices, some of which have long-standing consequences. The game isn’t a traditional soulslike, but with the difficulty and mechanics behind the game, it certainly feels like one.

Wolf is given a choice towards the back half of the game where he can either follow Iron Code or save Kuro. Following the code results in Wolf fully becoming a demon and killing many of the people he knows and cares about.

With interesting characterization and backstories, these are the JRPGs Where the Villain Feels More Compelling Than the Hero.

The premise of the game seems to frame your character as the hero, but in true FromSoftware fashion, you can become the villain. Featuring a morality tracker, the more you kill innocents and do vile deeds, the closer you become to being Pure Black.

At the end of the game, players can decide to simply betray their allies up to that point, killing them and thrusting the world into a new age of darkness. Whether you were the villain throughout the game or not, at the end there’s no debating it.

Vampires are pretty much always the bad guys, although when it comes to Dr. Jonathan Reid, players can decide what happens. Whether he succumbs to the monster within or maintains some semblance of humanity is in the hands of players.

Whatever path the player takes determines what happens to London and its people. Leaning into the destructive nature of vampires leaves the city in complete collapse and causes the epidemic to continue unfettered.

Final Fantasy games as a whole have always been a bit out there in terms of story, but unlike the other games on this list, you are literally the villain. Playing as Jack along with the other Strangers as you attempt to stop Chaos from destroying the world.

By the end of the story, there’s only one option for our heroes, and that’s for Jack to embrace the Chaos and become the villain of the story. This sends him back in time and sets him up as Garland, the villain of the first Final Fantasy game.

If you're bad to the bone, then check out these 8 Games Where Evil Is The Only Option.

#4392. Love and Deepspace 5.0 update brings together all five love interests for the first time

Love and Deepspace is getting a big update to celebrate its second anniversary, and there's a lot to dig through.

If you can believe it, Love and Deepspace is almost two-years-old, and Infold Games is celebrating the moment in a few major ways. The Throne of Eros update brings the game up to version 5.0, and it’s one for fans of all love interests.

For one, this is the first time all five of them are brought together. The update is also adding some important new features, alongside anniversary events, and more.

Throne of Eros also doubles as the new Wish Pool, which is the one that has all of the game’s love interests in a single banner. This is a limited-time affair, of course, but it’s not the only thing you should look forward to here.

There’s also the Memory Growth Bonus, another limited-time event that you can take advantage of to grow your Memories. The even bigger news is that you can target your Wishes through the Xspace Echo, which lets you select five Memories to create your own pool from. You can use this to get any Memories you might not have, of course.

On the topic of Memories, you’ll also be able to unlock new second anniversary KV Memories, as part of a Yearly Highlights Event that will let you look back on your own journey with the game over the past year.

On the story and narrative side, Throne of Eros adds two new main stories, with new branches for Xavier, and Rafayel. There’s even a narrative-specific event that will run throughout the anniversary period, through which you can earn two daily outfits for each of the five love interests.

The celebrations also extend to new anniversary content like mail, and video calls. You can purchase a Yearly Pass, and check out some new arrivals at the Lunar Shop.

Beyond the anniversary content, version 5.0 also adds a new feature to the game: Home, which essentially offers a hub to get you directly to interacting with love interests that doesn’t have to do with combat or story.

You can also expect various other quality of life updates that touch on the Journal, Phone Moments Search, Resources Quick Cleanup, and new Tete-a-Tete that should make interacting with all of them more streamlined.

While this is a special banner, you should brush up on how banners work in Love and Deepspace if you’re unfamiliar. As always, it’s never not a good idea to check our Love and Deepspace codes page for some freebies.

#4391. ‘Billie’ Is a 650-HP Modified Pontiac GTO from Ringbrothers

Ringbrothers is back at SEMA with a customized 1965 Pontiac, featuring carbon-fiber bodywork and an LT4 supercharged V-8 engine.

The 2026 SEMA show opened today, celebrating the unbridled imagination of the custom car scene, and, of course, Wisconsin-based Ringbrothers has returned with yet another exquisite creation. This year’s showpiece is a 1965 Pontiac GTO convertible dubbed “Billie,” which enhances the classic muscle car’s assertive styling and packs it with modern power.

Ringbrothers built Billie for a customer who wanted to pay tribute to a GTO his mother once owned. The client originally proposed the name “Goat,” with Ringbrothers suggesting Billie (as in billy goat), a more playful take on the iconic Pontiac’s long-held nickname.

See all results for used cars for sale near 30213

Despite presenting as a GTO, Billie originally started life as a 1965 Pontiac Tempest, before Ringbrothers went to work, widening the body by five inches, reshaping the front fenders, lengthening the rocker panels, and adding carbon-fiber doors. The hood is also fashioned from carbon fiber and wears billet-aluminum inserts and an enlarged scoop to feed air to the engine.

That engine is Chevy’s LT4 supercharged 6.2-liter V-8, cranking out 650 horsepower and 650 pound-feet of torque and hooked up to a Bowler Performance 10-speed automatic transmission. The body is placed atop a Roadster Shop Fast Track Stage III chassis, and Billie also features Fox coil-over springs and six-piston Brembo brakes. The staggered HRE G-Code wheels, measuring 19 inches up front and 20 inches at the rear, are shod in Michelin Pilot Sport Cup 2 rubber.

At first glance, Billie looks quite faithful to the original GTO, but look closely, and you’ll notice custom bumpers, new headlight surrounds, and a single-piece machined billet-aluminum taillight panel. Ringbrothers also employed carbon fiber on the lower front end and for the rear bumper section that houses the large exhaust outlets. Adding to the head-turning look is the Billie Goat Blue paint job, a rich, shimmering hue that is contrasted by polished chrome trim.

The cabin is outfitted in gray and blue leather, while the dashboard has been pushed four inches forward and two inches lower. Ringbrothers modernized the instrumentation, fitted a new climate-control system, and added an auto-dimming rearview mirror. There’s also a restored factory radio that now has Bluetooth connectivity, and the aluminum trim is paired with a sweet wood shifter.

Ringbrothers says the entire build took more than 5500 hours. Billie may not be as radical as some of Ringbrothers’ past projects, such as the LT4-powered Rolls-Royce dubbed “Paramount” or “Enyo,” a 1948 Chevy truck turned into an open-wheel race car, but the modified Pontiac is the perfect representation of the company’s expertise in honing the classic lines of vintage muscle cars.

As if the Ford Megazilla crate engine wasn’t already crazy enough at 7.3 liters of displacement, the Megazilla 2.0 engine added a 3.0-liter Whipple supercharger to the equation, unlocking over 1,000 horsepower. But now Ford Racing Parts has taken the recipe even further, showing off a new take on Megazilla 2.0 at the 2026 SEMA Show. Crammed under the hood of a Bronco dubbed Frostwarden is “the most powerful crate engine ever created by an automaker,” boasts Ford, producing over 1,200 hp and over 1,000 lb-ft of torque, and it’s taken a lot of extra engineering to ensure the engine can deliver those numbers reliably.

Ford is quick to point out that creating Megazilla 2.0 wasn’t as simple as bolting a supercharger to Megazilla 1.0, noting that the program required developing a stronger block, a camshaft specifically designed to work with a supercharger, beefier pistons, bigger fuel injectors, a different belt drive and damper, and the Gen 6 version of Whipple’s 3.0-liter blower, with a bright blue painted cover. But an engine sitting on a stand in a SEMA hall struggles to stand out, impressive as it may be, and that’s why the Frostwarden Bronco was built. The idea was based around a Bronco used for search and rescue operations in Arctic conditions, and that means the off-roader needed more than just a glow-up under the hood.

In association with Kincer Chassis in Tennessee, the widened Bronco was given portal gear lifts from 74Weld, custom 18-inch Weld bead-lock wheels wrapped in 42-inch BFGoodrich rubber, steel bumpers (with a winch in front), and custom Bilstein dampers. Driveline hardware was upgraded with help from Dana, and various accessories were added to the roof and tailgate, including traction board holders from RTR and extra lighting from Rigid. With a black-and-mustard theme on the exterior, the cabin was given similar treatment, along with additional carbon fiber highlights. Altogether, it looks as good as an OEM vehicle that might be offered on a dealer floor, and we quite like the dual-exit exhaust tips, but the Frostwarden, like other SEMA concepts, is not destined for series production.

The Frostwarden is basically one big, expensive advertisement for Ford Racing Parts and the scope of customization open to the Blue Oval’s products, but the main focus is undoubtedly this wild new version of the Megazilla supercharged V8. While a production vehicle with such an engine may not be feasible, builds like this help enthusiasts envision what is possible in a Ford, encouraging drag racers, drifters, off-roaders, and more to explore buying a one-size-fits-all engine regardless of their specific motoring application. So what does it cost? Ford has not said, but a naturally aspirated Megazilla 1.0 starts well over $20,000, and a 3.0-liter Whipple supercharger costs anything from $7,000 to $15,000, so Megazilla 2.0 will surely be in the $30k bracket.

#4389. Track-Optimized Fluidity: We Drive the 2027 Ariel Atom 4RR

With 525 horsepower on tap, the no-nonsense Atom 4RR could easily be overwhelming, but it isn’t.

When the Ariel Atom launched around the turn of the millennium, probably no one imagined that the lightweight British track car would evolve into the 4RR model of today—a 525-hp road-legal range topper based on the fourth-generation Atom and launched to celebrate the original’s 25th anniversary. In fact, the roughly 1500-pound “Double R” might be hard for U.S. buyers to conceive of, as only some lesser Ariel vehicles had been available stateside under a manufacturing licensing arrangement.

An exclusive new deal between Ariel and long-standing U.S. distributor Forman Motorworks changes that, with all Ariels and optional equipment now available to order via Forman for U.K. factory build slots. Customer deliveries in the U.S. are planned to start next summer.

The lineup includes the 4RR seen here, which is both the most powerful Atom ever and the most expensive at £208,000 in the U.K. (U.S. prices have yet to be confirmed, but we’d estimate $325,000.) That’s more than double the price of a very generously optioned 400-hp 4R model.

See all results for used cars for sale near 43207

Lower yourself into the Atom’s molded composite driving seat, thumb the start button, and feel the hand-built Civic Type R–derived turbo four-cylinder fizz through the steel-tube-frame chassis. Admittedly, the thought of blasting over the hedged lanes near Ariel’s rural base in Somerset, England, is more than a little intimidating. Yet even as the 4RR accelerates ferociously and telegraphs mechanical and road-surface detail like few other cars can, the big surprise is just how calm this extreme Atom feels.

Whether it’s the car’s refusal to be upset by midcorner bumps and awkward road cambers, or the drivability of the highly boosted turbo four, there’s an unexpected maturity and polish at play here. Even the Quaife six-speed sequential transmission can be soothed with a gentle brush of the clutch pedal. A handful of miles in, and our trepidation has already melted away.

Two things explain the 4RR’s fine road manners. The first is the clearly accomplished setup work overseen by race driver and former Top Gear Stig Phil Keen, and the second is some very expensive engineering.

The latter element includes reworked manually adjustable Öhlins dampers—which allowed Ariel to soften the inboard, pushrod-operated suspension—alongside a new aerodynamics package and 12.2-inch AP Racing brakes with four-piston calipers all around.

But the biggest investment involves the engine. Ariel doesn’t typically touch engine internals, but the 4RR’s previous-generation Civic Type R K20C unit has been completely reworked, blueprinted, and balanced in a process said to consume around 100 hours. Upgrades include forged connecting rods and pistons, closed-deck sleeves, and a revised cylinder head with improved camshafts, valve springs, and guides. A larger turbocharger runs nearly 25 psi of boost and is fed by an intercooler about twice the size of the 4R’s.

See all results for used cars for sale near 43207

The marquee numbers: 525 horsepower at 8200 rpm and 406 pound-feet of torque at 5200 revs. However, two tamer performance maps let you ease into it; there’s a 4R-matching 400-hp tune, as well as an intermediate 500-hp setting. Traction control and ABS are included and very welcome, both being driver adjustable through multiple stages, including fully off.

For such a small turbo four capable of producing so much power, the 4RR is disarmingly flexible at low revs and surprisingly progressive when it comes on boost, partly thanks to peak torque arriving at a far higher engine speed than in most modern turbocharged road cars.

That’s true in both the first two engine maps (despite the very noticeable step up in performance, including the intermediate map’s more substantial midrange boost), but it’s the seemingly modest 25-hp increase to the third and most powerful tune that transforms the experience. Still progressive and really quite tractable, it’s the searing, angry spit toward the 8200-rpm rev limiter that’s most noticeable, along with equally furious overrun pops. Throw in a few full-throttle, clutchless upshifts, and this amounts to delirious performance that—while usable on the road—is best reserved for an open racetrack.

Even then, traction from the 255-section rear tires is astonishing, at least in the hot, dry conditions of our drive. Whether launched off the line or subjected to a surge of midrange torque, the 4RR simply digs in and grips, thanks in no small part to compliant damping, sticky Yokohama A052 track-oriented rubber, and the weight of that Honda four pressing the rear tires into the tarmac.

Back-to-back drives in the 4RR and one of the first Atoms underlines the comedic jump in performance, but it’s the finesse of the 4RR chassis that’s more revealing of the car’s quarter century of development. Delightfully tactile as the original is, each individual wheel jiggles over bumps, and the car quickly becomes unstable if you back out of the throttle midcorner.

The 4RR retains comparable tactility but dials out the chassis noise and lifts the Atom’s capabilities to another level. The steering is super responsive but refuses to tug over tricky surfaces, the car’s balance is throttle adjustable but more forgiving of midcorner lifts, and crushing braking performance tames the engine’s power without causing the front axle to weave. For a circuit-optimized machine, the 4RR is exceptionally fluid on the road.

It’s easy to get caught up in the 4RR’s extreme nature and its hypercar-like power-to-weight ratio, but the real takeaway is how thoroughly Ariel has harnessed its intensity, creating a car that feels engineered around its performance, not overwhelmed by it.

Dubbed Traveler on a Winter's Night, Luna 4 introduces three new playable characters, and brings back The Lantern Rite event to celebrate the beginning of the new year.

The first new arrival in Version Luna 4 is Columbina Hyposelenia, the Moon Maiden. Columbina is a 5-Star Hydro Catalyst wielder. Her kit revolves around supporting the squad via Lunar Reactions. She can trigger coordinated Lunar Reaction DMG, even when she’s off the field.

The Moon Maiden’s special ability, Lunar Domain, further boosts all Lunar Reactions by applying a DMG bonus, including summoning more thundercloud strikes for Lunar-Charged reactions. Columbina is also capable of converting Electro-Charged, Bloom, and Hydro Crystallize reactions into Lunar Reactions, as well as revive fallen squad members.

Speaking of elemental reactions, new in this version is Lunar-Crystallize, a new reaction that’s triggered when Geo meets Hydro (under certain conditions). When triggered, Lunar-Crystallize summons three Moondrifts near enemies. When triggered three times, Moondrift Harmony gets activated, dealing Geo DMG to enemies caught in its radius.

Then there’s Zibai, an Adeptus from Liyue. Zibai is another 5-Star character, a Geo Sword wielder. Zibai can, through entering a special state where they can build up energy, unleash an Elemental Skill that deals Lunar-Crystallize DMG.

The longer the fight goes on, the more Lunar-Crystallize reactions are triggered, the higher (and more often) the damage of Zibai’s Elemental Skill becomes.

Luna 4 continues the Nod-Krai story arc, with a big confrontation with Il Dottore. This is the focus of the new Archon Quest, completing which will earn you a new outfit. There’s a gameplay element to that new chapter, too, with the reveal of Piramida, a new area north of the region. Piramida is the headquarters of the Lightkeepers.

The first phase of Luna 4’s Event Wishes will, unsurprisingly, feature Columbina. It’ll also include reruns of Ineffa. The second phase is when Zibai becomes available, alongside another newcomer: Illuga, a 4-Star, polearm-wielding Geo Lightkeeper. The second phase’s rerun will be Neuvillette, who’s also going to have a new outfit in the shop at a discount.

Version Luna 4 brings back the annual Lantern Rite event, taking place in the mainland of Liyue. The event features its own set of minigames with unique rewards, alongside new stories of the Adepti.

All around Liyue Harbor, you’ll be able to place Xiao Lanterns and inscribe them with messages for others to read. You’ll also earn some Fortune Coins from Auspicious Treasure Trees, which you can later exchange for gifts.

All players will receive 1,600 Primogems through the in-game mail. If you log in regularly, you can earn up to ten Intertwined Fates. Lantern Rite has a new outfit for Yaoyao, which is also where you have a chance to earn one 4-Star Liyue character for free.

Finally, you can look forward to the new Classic Mode in Miliastra Wonderland, which lets you invite select Teyvat characters to join you.

Kia's Telluride Is Closing In On The Sportage's U.S. Sales Crown

Ford Crams The Most Powerful OEM Crate Engine Ever Made Into New Bronco Concept

Mercedes-Benz Wants To Blow Snow Off Your Car Before You Open The Door

A sixth consecutive month of record sales has Kia on a high, and it may soon have a new best-selling model.

Ford Crams The Most Powerful OEM Crate Engine Ever Made Into New Bronco Concept

Kia has built on an already tremendous growth streak in the United States with record October sales. With 80,008 vehicles sold last month, Kia posted its best-ever October sales, beating the previous record for that month by 16%. October also marked a sixth consecutive month of record sales for the Korean automaker. Most Kia models delivered year-over-year growth, and five models—including the second-generation Telluride—posted best-ever October sales.

From EVs to hybrids and conventional gas-powered models, Kia’s current lineup is proving to be a fine match for American tastes and budgets. In October, the brand also set new sales records for hybrids and electrified vehicles (including EVs), with hybrids alone increasing by 114%. The following Kia models achieved best-ever October sales:

In terms of year-over-year sales growth, the EV9 led the way, with sales of 1,406 units in October, an increase of 111%. In a year where total EV sales in the U.S. are down by roughly 30%, that’s a significant achievement. The new EV3 went on sale last quarter and tallied 976 sales in October, taking its total to 1,496 for the year.

“With six consecutive months of record-breaking sales, Kia is accelerating toward a fourth straight annual sales record, powered by the strength of our world-class model lineup and our nationwide network of retail partners,” said Eric Watson, vice president, sales operations, Kia America. “An expanding hybrid lineup, the arrival of the all-new, all-electric EV3, and the success of the all-new Telluride and Seltos are adding even more momentum to our growth. We’re confident this record-setting pace will carry us through the fourth quarter and well into 2027.”

One number that jumped out to us is the slim gap between the Sportage (traditionally Kia’s best-selling vehicle in the U.S.) and the Telluride in October. In October 2025, the Sportage was ahead of the Telluride by 7,486 units. That gap narrowed to only 3,968 models last month.

This change could come down to the fact that the Sportage is deep into its current life cycle and demand has tapered off slightly, whereas the Telluride is still fresh. If the current trends continue, Kia’s best-selling model could very well be the Telluride in a few months, despite it costing thousands more than the two-row Sportage.

Kia is killing it in the United States right now. While many automakers find success in just a few segments, what’s noticeable about Kia is that it’s growing across the board. Hybrids and EVs are thriving, while buyers have expressed increasing interest in the brand’s three-row crossovers, electric SUVs, minivans, and small hatchbacks/sedans. Kia’s growth is also outpacing the industry. According to Automotive News, automakers that have reported October sales results saw an overall 8.6% increase, but Kia alone is up by almost double that, at 16%. Kia also outsold Hyundai, its corporate sibling, for the third month in 2026.

#4386. CD Projekt Red Poaches Another Warhorse Lead

Melissa Sarnowski is a Gaming Writer at DualShockers who has been covering games professionally since 2022. She specializes in lists, reviews, and features, with additional experience writing guides for Hardcore Gamer. Before joining DualShockers, Melissa contributed to Screen Rant, and she currently writes for CBR and

CD Projekt Red continues to add talented developers to its team, particularly those who were working in lead roles at Warhorse Studios, as noticed by b0ysbrokenheart on X (formerly Twitter). The latest addition is Zbynek Zelinka, whom b0ysbrokenheart showed using a screenshot of Zelinka's LinkedIn profile showing his current job as a Senior Gameplay Designer at CD Projekt Red, starting in October 2026.

In an recent interview, it was discussed how The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt devs were initially told they could not make it.

Zelinka was previously a Lead Technical Designer at Warhorse Studios, where he worked for a total of seven years and 10 months, rising from Technical Designer to Senior Technical Designer and eventually Lead Technical Designer before departing for CD Projekt Red.

In addition to Zelinka, Zdenek Glatz and Karel Kolmann have also left Warhorse Studios for CD Projekt Red in the last year. All three of these developers were at Warhorse Studios for seven or eight years, meaning CD Projekt Red is picking up some highly experienced employees, at least two of whom have been involved in the development of both Kingdom Come: Deliverance and Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2.

Glatz joined CD Projekt Red in May 2026, according to his LinkedIn, as a Senior Open World Designer. Before that, he was a Lead Level Designer at Warhorse Studios, having previously worked as a Game Designer/Writer and Senior Game Designer/Writer at the studio. He's bringing eight and a half years of experience to CD Projekt Red with him.

In addition to Zelinka, Zdenek Glatz and Karel Kolmann have also left Warhorse Studios for CD Projekt Red in the last year.

Kolmann joined CD Projekt Red in November 2025 as a Senior Quest Designer. She spent just over eight years at Warhorse Studios before that, starting as a Writer and Game Designer in 2017, then moving to Senior Game Designer and eventually to Lead Gameplay Designer. With them together, CD Projekt Red gains a combined 24 years of game design experience to add to their in-progress projects.

CD Projekt Red has a few highly anticipated games in the works, and the company is clearly doing its best to grab talented developers to help bring those games to life. We know that CD Projekt Red is working on a sequel to Cyberpunk 2077, which has the placeholder name of Project Orion, and a job listing shows that they aren't finished searching for developers to help with the game.

Then, you have The Witcher 4 in development from CD Projekt Red, which continues the series by putting Ciri in the role of main character, and this project would be particularly fitting for the devs who left Warhorse Studios to work on it. The world of The Witcher has more magic and fantasy elements, but the general setting isn't that different from Kingdom Come: Deliverance. If I had to guess, I'd bet that the Witcher series is where the former Warhorse devs are going to be working.

They could also be put on The Witcher 3's Songs of the Past expansion's development team, but the release date for that is close enough that I imagine a lot of the development is finished, and it's in the final stages, which leaves The Witcher 4 as the most likely choice, or the secretive Project Hadar new IP that we don't really know anything about.

Meanwhile, Warhorse Studios has another Kingdom Come game in the works and a Lord of the Rings game, but the comments on b0ysbrokenheart's X post show that people are a bit worried about these games as devs are leaving the studio for CD Projekt Red. One even asked CD Projekt Red to "hold their horses" for the sake of the next Kingdom Come game so it can be as good as the first two.

I'm not very worried about the projects, as all the studio closures mean that there are, unfortunately, a ton of talented developers currently out of work, and I'm sure many of them would be a great fit to join Warhorse Studios.

#4384. Heartopia captures the hearts of Animal Crossing and The Sims fans to become the No.1 free download across 50 countries

Heartopia is officially the first big mobile launch of 2026, as the game grabs the attention of millions worldwide.

Heartopia, the new cosy life sim from XD Games, has officially arrived on mobile, right on schedule. If you’ve been keeping up with Heartopia news, you’re likely already aware that the game has pushed back its Steam release to an indeterminate point in 2026.

Doesn’t look like it mattered much, however, as this has already been a big launch on iOS and Android — it probably helps that PC players aren't being entirely left out of the fun, since the game is already available there via XD's own cross-device platform TapTap.

XD Games announced today that Heartopia has reached the top spot on the App Store’s downloads page for free games, and it managed to do so in more than 50 countries and regions worldwide.

The developer is celebratig by offering players a lot of free stuff. If you're feeling lucky, you’ll find new outfits and furniture in three gacha banners (Gilded Acorn Exhibitions): Polar Hymn, The Frostguard, and Coolplayism.

XD Games says you can expect regular updates to add more content, through Fashionwaves and Festivals. In fact, the first season - Winter Frost - is already penciled in for sometime in late January, and it’s going to add appropriately wintery activities like ice skating and snowman-building.

In February, a My Little Pony collaboration event will kick off, bringing new inspired outfits, and vehicles to the game.

Heartopia is a clever mix of Animal Crossing, and The Sims. It’s a free-to-play life sim where you can create your own character, dress them up, build a home for them (and decorate it), and go about town visiting and playing with other players’ characters.

The game’s main feature is the ability to take on a hobby, and seven of those are available at launch. You can dig deep into each hobby, either alone or with others, and there’s a progression track dedicated to each one.

Whether you’re among the millions who downloaded the game already, or you intend to so soon, we’ve got a set of helpful guides to get you started. You should check out how to unlock and upgrade hobbies in Heartopia first, before you get deep into finding all cooking recipes. And, of course, this wouldn’t be a big game launch without a bunch of Heartopia codes for some free stuff.

#4383. The Car That Fell to Earth: We Test the 1979 Datsun 310-GX

This little Datsun is still getting in touch with reality.

From the May 1979 issue of Car and Driver.

Datsun is not giving up its small-car territory without a fight. All the adver­tising miles on the new 310 are proof of that. For months now, you’ve seen Dat­sun’s new small car zipping across your TV screen, splashed lavishly over maga­zine pages, and blown up bigger than life on roadside billboards. If Datsun is driven to do anything, it’s to sell 310s.

This ad blitz is understandable, be­cause the 310 is Datsun’s new-genera­tion front-wheel-drive car, a key weapon it will use to defend itself in the world­wide small-car war that’s escalating vi­ciously even now. Moreover, it repre­sents Datsun’s second attempt at build­ing a front-drive sedan, since it’s the successor to the ill-fated F-10. As an ac­knowledged small-car giant, Datsun has a reputation to protect.

To these ends, Datsun has armed itself with a pair of all-new three-door se­dans. They’re named simply the 310 se­dan and the 310-GX—which is the sub­ject of this test. A four-door sedan may be sent over later, but for now, just these two constitute the 310 arsenal. The sedan is the family hauler, while the GX is intended to add a dose of sport to the basic 310 theme. For all practical purposes, the two cars are mechanically identical.

See all results for used cars for sale near 43228

The 310 shares its basic layout with the original F-10. It once again has a 1397 cc four-cylinder engine mounted transversely in the chassis and driving the front wheels. Each corner of the unit body is again suspended independently, with MacPherson struts, coil springs, and an anti-sway bar up front, and trail­ing arms and coil springs in the rear. But aside from these superficial similarities to the old F-10, the new 310 is, as they say, new from bumper to bumper.

Which is just fine by us, because the old F-10 just wasn’t suited to life here on spaceship earth. It was, you’ll re­member, an unearthly amalgam of fun­ny shapes and openings, a cramped and noisy little car that always acted a bit tipsy. In fact, given the way the packaging advantages of front-wheel drive were ignored in the F-10, it could well have been designed three thousand miles in outer space instead of that same distance across the Pacific. About the only things you could say in its favor were that its engine, proven in the B-210, was reliable and that it was good in the snow. Not exactly a rave review.

Datsun wants us to forget the past. It's made every attempt to mold the 310 into a car completely different from its predecessor. And if appearances are anything to go by, it’s accomplished that goal. The old banana-with-windows styling has given way to a fresh-cut wedge profile. And while Datsun hasn’t made the 310 any lower, it has made it longer and noticeably wider. For the record, it’s five inches longer and four inches wider, but—at 2600 pounds­—only 80 pounds heavier. Inside, the handsome velour seats, thick carpeting, and color-keyed dash bespeak a new­found awareness of American tastes. And, standard procedure for Japanese carmakers, Datsun has loaded the 310 chock-full of features designed to make life behind the wheel more pleasant.

See all results for used cars for sale near 43228

Every 310, GX or sedan, comes with reclining seats, a split-back folding rear seat, a slider mechanism that moves the passenger’s bucket forward to facilitate rear-seat entry, a quartz clock, a remote hatch opener, side-window defroster vents, intermittent wipers, power brakes, a remote fuel-filler-door open­er, a rear defogger, and a day-night mir­ror. The sedan also features console-­mounted remote cable controls for the flip-out rear windows. The GX adds roll-down rear quarter-windows, a rear window wiper-washer, a tach, a five­-speed transmission, a four-spoke steer­ing wheel, and fatter, 165/70-13 tires. It certainly seems as though Datsun has wedged the 310 right into the heart of small-car country. Yet despite such favorable first impressions, we found—af­ter living with a GX for more than 2000 miles—that all is still not well with Dat­sun’s front-drive car.

The small-car facts of life have been readily defined for Datsun by such front-line front-drivers as the Rabbit, the Strada, the Omni/Horizon, the Fies­ta, the Civic, and now GM’s formidable new X-body compacts. But when you compare it with its competition, the 310 comes off as little more than an F-10 that fell to earth and isn’t quite in touch with reality yet.

The 310’s interior is a perfect exam­ple of the confusing inconsistencies that compromise the car throughout. Datsun obviously went to a lot of trouble to make the 310’s cabin more hospitable than the F-10’s, yet the effect of the handsome carpeting, dash, and uphol­stery is offset by door panels that look plain enough to have come out of a Dat­sun pickup. Datsun also widened the car to achieve more interior width. This al­leviates the phone-booth claustropho­bia of the F-10—but only for front-seat passengers; rear-seat riders are almost as cramped as they were in the older car. In both new cars, rear legroom is still in severely short supply. Other front-drive cars with the same wheel­base do much better in this respect.

Where the GX really falls down on the job is in the all-important area of day-to-day livability. The 310 is so rid­dled with annoying quirks that its posi­tive qualities are overshadowed.

Take the radio, for instance. Please. Our test car had the optional AM/FM unit. Besides impoverished reception, it was endowed with what has to be one of this decade’s worst speakers—mounted under the dash, facing the floor. Most of the music we could tune in became bad­ly garbled when the volume was turned up loud enough to be heard during highway cruising. You don’t have to lis­ten to the radio, of course, but you’ll find the heating system harder to avoid. When you do use it, you’ll find it only marginally effective. Worse yet, the de­froster—which has to work overtime to get the job done—is about as quiet as an idling 747.

And if you want a little whine before dinner, the 310’s trans­mission will be more than happy to oblige—in any gear. Though the 310’s shift linkage is much improved over the F-10’s Silly Putty unit, the transmission crunched almost every time we grabbed third gear. Then there’s the matter of the shift pattern, which has first down and to the left, off of the H, and re­verse—with no protective lockout­—dead ahead, where any self-respecting low gear ought to be. And sure enough, there is the occasional gnashing of re­verse when making the one-two shift.

Then again, we didn’t like reverse much anyway, because selecting it brought on the annoying warning beeper that is Datsun’s fix for the shift-pattern prob­lem. (It’s there to prevent the unwary from backing away from stoplights when they put the shifter where first is in most other cars.) Last but not least was the vibration problem. At idle, the GX’s engine was so rough that the steering wheel actually got a little blurry around the edges. Nudging the idle up about 100 rpm would solve that prob­lem, but only the engineers will be able to quiet the sharp buzzing of the ex­haust system as the revs climb past 5000—a sound that is the essence of tin­niness. Most of these problems also cropped up on a 310 sedan we were sampling, so they seem to be basic de­sign flaws, not isolated failings of the GX test car.

All of this, when added to the below­ average space utilization, makes the 310 rough-edged—even crude—given the current level of small-car sophistication. That’s unfortunate, because it’s due cause for avoiding what is essentially a fun car to drive. The little engine revs up willingly, and the five-speed—top gear is a direct 1:1 ratio—helps you make good use of the available power. The steering response is direct, and there’s plenty of road feel. Once you get used to the suspension’s initial rubberi­ness when you first twist the wheel, the GX turns out to be a fine fling-around car. It’s also quite stable during highway cruising, and it rides acceptably as well. And of course it’s stingy with your gas money, returning 27 miles for every EPA gallon.

But decent road manners are only part of what makes a good small car. The 310 represents a Datsun move in the right direction, but little more; that it’s superior to the F-10 is frankly not one of the world’s outstanding accom­plishments. This is underscored by the fact that $5500 will probably also buy a well-equipped GM X-body compact. And the 310 can’t begin to match the X­ car’s room, ride, quietness, appoint­ments, and overall refinement—yet its economy is only marginally better. The 310 isn’t in the same league.

So at this point the best news we have is that Datsun’s front-drive car has final­ly come down to earth. But if it’s to live here happily, Datsun will have to try still harder—a lot harder.

Since the subject of this test is the 310 sport coupe, I’ll have to add my vote to the negative side. And that’s too bad, be­cause condemning the sport coupe can, by extension, condemn the sedan that came, afterthought-like, with the deal. My strongest negatives about the sport coupe are its looks (really ugly) and its transmission (really terrible). I don’t have either of those complaints about the sedan. In fact, I think Datsun’s marketeers are in for a surprise. Despite their studied predictions, my hunch is the sporty version will be shunned in the showroom (”Yes, Harry. It’s true. It’s the dreaded Show­room Shun”), and the boxy but cute, sim­ple but contemporary sedan will find favor. And that’s the way it should be, be­cause the 310 sedan is—in the Datsun tradition—a functional, sensible, straightfor­ward transportation module, and that’s what a lot of people are looking for these days. They don’t want an overstyled, beeping aggravation. —Mike Knepper

The Datsun 310, like the Subaru, makes us wonder if there is not a streak of automotive perversity loose among America’s car buyers, and if Datsun may not be on to something big. The 310 simply does not address itself to creature comfort in the way that a Toyota or a Honda does. It is a rather Spartan car, with lots of engine and transmission noise, and very little iso­lation from the mechanical realities. There’s an old-fashioned rough-and­-readiness about the 310 that’s not masked by velour upholstery or cut-pile carpets­—a sort of naïve innocence that appealed to me, along with my belief that it would probably run forever—but I couldn’t ex­plain my affectionate regard for these attributes to my co-testers. Noisy little cars that bucket along as the Datsun does are fun. They bring out an adolescent streak in me that 30 years of automotive experi­ence has been insufficient to suppress. They are amusingly likable in their imper­fections—the four-speed sedan more so than the more pretentious coupe. The 310 didn’t try to kid me, nor did it ever let me down. Only when I learned how much I’d have to pay for those simple, earthy pleasures did my enthusiasm start to flag. —David E. Davis Jr.

#4382. Diablo 4's long-awaited Tower and its Leaderboards enter beta today, and there's no PTR funny business this time

Diablo 4's first big moment of 2026 is nearly upon us, and it's one feature many have been looking forward to for actual years.

Diablo 4 is about to deliver on Blizzard’s years-old promise to add a challenging, leaderboard-driven experience to the action RPG. The beta for The Tower, and its associated Leaderboards are about to kick off.

As recently revealed, the new experience launches today at 11am PT, 2pm ET, 7pm GMT. This is a beta version that arrives alongside update 2.5.2.

This early launch won’t offer the full experience, and it’s mainly designed to get it into the hands of players early so that Blizzard could get as much feedback as possible and incorporate it into the final version.

The beta is available to everyone, which is a nice change from the usual rigmarole players would have to go through to get the PTR build and play on a different branch. The Tower, and Leaderboards will be available only in the Seasonal Realm, however. Indeed, the plan is to build on what’s there with each future season, so it’s best to think of it as a seasonal experience.

The Tower is about as simple of an activity as you can get in an action RPG. The goal is to climb as many floors as you can as quickly as you can, all while battling increasingly difficult mobs.

You need to reach and beat the Tower’s final boss before you can call it a run. The Leaderboard will then show your time, and let you see how well you did compared to other players.

The Tower is available to anyone who completed Rank 2 of the current Season Rank. Once done, an Obelisk will appear in Cerrigar, letting you access the challenge.

The Leaderboards themselves will operate on a two-week schedule, all of which will take place during a given season. In this case, they’re going to close the day before Season of the Divine Interversion - the game’s current season - ends.

Blizzard published an updated set of patch notes that show how much has changed since The Tower, and Leaderboards first became playable in the patch 2.5.0 PTR.

#4381. 10 Weirdest Missions in Borderlands 4

Aden Carter is a Contributor at DualShockers who has been covering games professionally since 2020. He specializes in lists and guides, with a focus on RPGs, horror games, survival horror, Soulslikes, cozy/sim games, and action-adventure titles. Before joining DualShockers, Aden contributed to GameRant, XDA, Gamepur, I

Gearbox has never shied away from adding weird characters and missions in their games. For instance, Borderlands 2 had a mission where your only goal was to shoot a guy named Face McShooty in the face.

There are plenty of weapons in Borderlands 4 that have been added in DLC. Which ones of them are the best?

The developers rely on weird and unhinged comedy to help them sell the worlds they create, and Kairos is a rather interesting world with some interesting inhabitants that require your aid.

You might be tasked with proving that the world is flat, or maybe you need to go on a treasure hunt. No matter what though, you will be asked to perform some rather odd tasks in Borderlands 4.

Out in the Fadefields, you can find a missile that didn’t explode when it hit the ground. The missile’s name is Gigi, and she just wants to see if she can explode, as that is her purpose in life.

As you collect parts to rebuild the missile to place Gigi’s core into, she confides in you that she wishes to never be a dud. Through the mission, your vault hunter consoles Gigi, giving her hope that she may explode just like she wants.

In the end, you rebuild the rocket, fire it off into the distance, and let Gigi discover her one true purpose in life. It’s a weird mission to be sure, but a strangely hope-filled one that can touch the heart.

Have you ever taken a moment to think that the world might be flat? Well, there are many who have thought that, and many who still do, and Gearbox acknowledges that with the Flat Kairoser mission.

During this mission, you meet a guy named Skeptical Sam. He happens to be standing next to a vehicle with signs that read, “Kairos is flat,” and has a rather unique appearance.

Throughout the mission, you perform some interesting tasks to try and prove that Kairos is flat and not round like everyone else thinks. For instance, you smash a globe, and you travel to a shrine to see the “curvature” of Kairos. You are then required to prove that Kairos isn’t flat to completely debunk everything Sam believes.

Have you ever received a mission from a toilet with a sentient AI placed inside it? No? Well, you are about to, as that is what happens in the Potty Mouth mission in Borderlands 4.

GenIVIV from Borderlands 3 has made a return, and her AI has been placed inside of a toilet. She asks you to deal with miscreants around Carcadia Burn who mistreat her.

Once you talk to the mayor, however, you find out that GenIVIV has been a pain in the butt for everyone in the literal sense. After this, you must call upon ClapTrap with the Clap Signal and try to find a new body for GenIVIV. It is a hilariously strange quest with quite a few twists and turns.

The series is so brilliantly strange that it was difficult to choose the 10 Wildest Borderlands Side Quests.

Legendary singer Rodd Vomit, who you have obviously heard of, didn’t survive his crash landing onto Kairos. Therefore, the band Thrum Dumpster needs a new lead singer, and Lisa FullFolja needs you to track down some potential candidates.

You need to travel across Carcadia Burn to find a few different singers, attach Digi-Dongles to them, and then return to The Couch Hole. It’s a relatively straightforward mission, but it culminates in a musical mosh pit that makes it rather strange.

The band turns hostile, and you need to deal with it. It’s okay though, because Lisa reveals that was the plan all along, and that it was all done for clout.

You’ve heard of escape rooms before, but you’ve probably never experienced a no-escape room. It is a room that is designed to kill you if you get the answers wrong, and you need to help test it out.

You find the No-Escape Room mission in the Terminus District of Dominion, and it is a rather bizarre experience. Once you enter, the Smiley Man will have you attempt to complete the different rooms.

Of course, you can complete them the normal way, or you can cheat your way to victory. Along the way, you need to guess the correct door, go through a maze, and place symbols in order. All of this is done while a madman is talking to you.

Borderlands 4 has plenty of references to pop culture, and the Wayward Gun mission is one of them. It is also a bizarre quest that has you interacting with guns in a way you might not expect.

If you have ever wondered what it would be like to play Pokémon in Borderlands, then this mission is for you. After a group of Tediore weapons get loose, you are tasked with catching them all in storage containers.

You are given containers to throw like PokéBalls, and there is even a version of Team Rocket that appears to try and stop you. It is a surreal experience, but one that definitely stands out among the other missions in the game.

Borderlands may have bazillions of guns, but these ten are the weirdest ones around.

Do you remember Face McShooty in Borderlands 2? He was the guy that you need to shoot in the face. Well, there is a reference to this mission in Borderlands 4, and it is rather weird. Instead of shooting a guy, you crack a guy’s back.

In Terminus Range, you can come across a man named Crack McBacky, and you need to crack his back as the name of the mission implies. However, the crick in his back is rather persistent, and won’t be dealt with easily.

Throughout the mission, you need to consistently melee his back. Just when you think he has received the relief he wants, you need to crack it again. This keeps going until you jump off a literal cliff and slam his back.

Have you ever thought that maybe your calling in life was to help others receive spiritual enlightenment? Well, that is what you are trying out in the Next Quest Thing mission in Borderlands 4.

A Wayward Soul wants you to help give them spiritual guidance. Of course, you are not a guru of any sort, so you will need to improvise. During the mission, you make up a lot of different tasks for the Wayward Soul to complete to give him spiritual enlightenment.

He wants balance, so you balance a trash can lid on his head. At a certain point, the guy even tries to be friends with a Ripper.

Sure, murder, mayhem, and chaos are all fun, but they get stale after a while. Sometimes, you need to find something else to do on Kairos, so why not try out some practical jokes?

That is the premise of the Imminent Jest mission, as you are recruited to help a Ripper perform some little pranks. Jankus wants to prank Crankus, so you shoot a pipe to get ooze all over Crankus.

Of course, now it is Crankus’ turn to prank Jankus … by setting him on fire. These harmless pranks don’t turn out to be so harmless, but it is a weird quest that takes a bit of a break from the nonstop violence of Borderlands 4, making it memorable and strange.

At a certain point in your travels around Kairos, you may come across a man surrounded by Threshers. This man is named Mort, and he has a desire to breed some Threshers, and you need to help him out with this strange request.

First, you are tasked with collecting a few Thresher eggs. This isn’t the weird part. The weird part comes when you get back to Mort’s shack and see that it is covered in hearts. It even has a sign that reads, “Hump hut.”

After delivering the eggs, he hatches one, calls the Thresher Daisy, and then proceeds to tell you to help her attract a mate. From here on out, it is weird, there is mood music involved, and plenty of pulsating tentacles. Gearbox got weird with this one.

Pop culture references are a baked-in part of the Borderlands games, but these ten are the greatest.

#4379. 1985 Ford F-250 Restomod Sends Raptor Brand to the ’80s at SEMA

Matt Johnson’s 1985 F-250 Raptor-inspired build was backed by Ford Performance and will be part of Ford’s display at SEMA this year.

Ford’s first Raptor didn’t arrive until 2008 at the 41st Baja 1000 in Ensenada, Mexico. The high-performance F-150 SVT Raptor-R had a podium finish, and the Raptor name continues to grace the widened bodywork of some of Ford’s most powerful pickups.

But imagine if Raptor had come around about two decades earlier. It might’ve looked like Matt Johnson’s Raptor-inspired 1985 F-250, which is getting a huge reveal at Ford’s SEMA booth this year.

The F-250 project actually started with an old Toyota Land Cruiser, which Johnson had planned to put an EcoBoost engine into. A call to Ford Racing Parts led to discussions about a collaboration between the automaker and Johnson, who restores older off-roading vehicles and documents the process on social media.

See all results for new 2027 Ford Super Duty for sale near 99501

A few months later, Ford suggested putting a small-block Heritage motor in the Land Cruiser. Johnson bounced back with a photo of a 1985 F-250 with a blown engine that had been sitting behind his shop. He felt the small-block was better suited for a classic Ford, and the bullnose F-250 seemed like a perfect candidate.

Soon, Johnson’s $800 shop truck, called Norma Jeane, was getting a full makeover backed by Ford Performance. The truck’s original engine was replaced with Ford Racing’s 575-hp 460-cubic-inch Boss V-8. He paired the small-block with a Ford R680 six-speed automatic transmission.

Johnson documented the transformation through a 92-part series on social media. His daily updates covered everything, from installing a custom-made suspension kit to weatherstripping the windows. Though a lot of the truck is now brand new, the F-250 maintains its distinctly ‘80s qualities, right down to the hubcaps and vintage-style stereo.

The build was originally meant to be completed in 40 days, but when Ford proposed the idea of bringing it to SEMA, that 40-day timeline shifted to a much longer saga. Along the way, Johnson has accumulated 425,000 followers on Instagram and even more on Facebook under his Doc Johnson Restorations shop account. His latest post shows the F-250 getting loaded into a transport truck and beginning the journey from his small shop in Klamath Falls, Oregon, to SEMA in Las Vegas.

“Honestly, it’s a crazy story, and I feel blessed to be a part of it,” Johnson said in a press release. “The truck—and the project itself—took on a life of its own. In many ways, I’m just along for the ride.” Johnson and his Raptor-inspired F-250 will be a part of Ford’s display at SEMA, which takes place November 3-6 in Las Vegas, Nevada.

#4378. The Sims developer vows "our values are unchanged," as it teases multiple projects from post-Saudi-owned EA

The team behind one of EA's most diverse franchises has issued a statement about its future under the soon-to-be Saudi-owned publisher.

In their (slightly belated) new years message to players, the developer of EA’s The Sims series of games has lightly addressed concerns about its future within the publisher in a wide-ranging letter to the community.

The letter also serves as something of a light plan for what players can expect soon, and in the future, alongside what the various teams are currently working on.

The developer starts off the yearly check-in with a statement that attempts to address concerns about the future of The Sims, historically one of EA’s most inclusive and culturally diverse franchises.

This, of course, comes in the wake of last year’s bombshell that EA is being taken private by a coalition led by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF), alongside investment firms Silver Lake Capital and Affinity Partners. The $55 billion acquisition was approved by EA’s shareholders in December, and is set to close by the end of June.

Understandably, many raised concerns about what EA’s new ownership would mean for its people, and portfolio of games. The news is concerning for The Sims in particular, a series that’s long embraced diversity and inclusivity, and has historically been popular among women, people of colour, and members of the LGBTQ+ community.

“Our Sims team's creative control, guided by our values of inclusivity, choice, creativity, community, and play, has not changed,” the post reads, though without referring to the buyout directly at any point.

“These values inspire the decisions we make each and every day as we plan for today, tomorrow, and the future.”

As for what’s to come in 2026 and beyond, it sounds like The Sims team has multiple irons in the fire. The developer is working on “a family of new Sims experiences” that will find homes on PC, console, and mobile. Crucially, the post says that not every experience will be on every platform, in order for each to focus on delivering something different and interesting.

Future releases, of course, include new The Sims 4 content that focuses on the single-player experience. The social and more multiplayer-driven experiences, however, will instead be found in Project Rene, the mobile-first life-sim currently in development. (Despite early confidence that it was a working title for The Sims 5, it's now confirmed that Project Rene won’t, in fact, be a direct successor to The Sims 4.)

Some of these projects will see more playtesting throughout 2026, so you should probably sign up for The Sims Labs if you want to hear about when/how you can get involved.

#4377. 2027 Harley-Davidson Sprint 440 Harkens Back to a Simpler Time

Harley-Davidson’s new entry-level motorcycle resurrects a classic name and its single-cylinder formula.

Given the price of, well, everything these days, affordability and accessibility are unsurprisingly hot buzzwords in the motorcycle industry. And brands that’ve embraced them are reaping the benefits. Bikes like Triumph’s 400 range and Royal Enfield’s 350 range—lightweight, inexpensive, modest-capacity single-cylinder—are practically flying off showroom floors. Up until now, that’s described nothing in Harley-Davidson’s stable, at least for US riders. But that changes with the 2027 Harley-Davidson Sprint 440.

See all results for used cars for sale near 33801

While the Bar and Shield basically bleeds V-twins, the brand hasn’t only made two-cylinder bikes. Its earliest models, often called “Silent Gray Fellows,” had single-cylinder engines. And if the new Sprint 440’s name seems familiar to you, it’s because Harley sold single-powered bikes with that nameplate in the 1960s and 1970s.

While those Sprints were built in Italy, the US-market Sprint 440s will be built in Harley’s York, Pennsylvania factory. Admittedly, this new Sprint technically derives from the single-cylinder Harley that’s already been on sale elsewhere for several years: the X440 developed together with the Indian company Hero MotoCorp. But still, don’t cry heresy, Milwaukee faithful.

It might use a vintage name and manufacturing formula, but the 2027 Sprint 440 is a thoroughly modern Harley-Davidson. Its 440cc two-valve air/oil-cooled single-cylinder engine—fuel-injected, unlike the carbureted original Sprints—makes 27 hp and 28 pound-feet, sent to the rear wheel via a slip-assist clutch and six-speed transmission. That rear wheel is 17 inches in diameter, with the front being 19 inches; both are cast aluminum. And when the Sprint needs to stop, er, sprinting, you’ve got ABS-equipped disc brakes.

If that doesn’t seem like enough scream for this eagle, know that the Royal Enfield Meteor 350 cruiser’s 394cc single-cylinder engine makes 20 hp and 20 pound-feet. Also, according to the spec sheets, the Sprint 440 is slightly lighter: a claimed 412 pounds to the Meteor 350’s 421 pounds. The Sprint is that much lighter than the upcoming Triumph Bonneville T40 as well, though the Triumph’s 398cc liquid-cooled single makes 30 hp (and other Triumph 400 models make around 40 hp). But, in another accessibility nod, the Meteor 350’s and Bonneville T4’s seats are 30.1 and 32.2 inches high, respectively, while Harley claims a 26.4-inch laden seat height for the Sprint. All three of these bikes have preload-adjustable dual rear shocks, though unlike the other two, the Sprint 440’s forks are inverted.

See all results for used cars for sale near 33801

Moving on, the 2027 Harley-Davidson Sprint 440 has a color TFT display (something quickly becoming de rigeur). The 3.5-inch circular gauge shows a speedometer, tachometer, odometer, and trip meter as well as the usual warning lights and turn signals. Those turn signals, like the headlight and taillight, are LED. And there’s one of the other modern motorcycling necessities, a USB-C charging port, above the headlight. Additionally, Harley-Davidson will offer numerous accessories for the Sprint 440, including a windshield, engine guard, saddlebags, and (predictably) skull adornments. Also, if the regular seat isn’t the right height, there will be multiple seat options to dial in your proper fit.

OK, accessibility seems fine, but what about that affordability? When Harley-Davidson first announced it was resurrecting the Sprint, it claimed the bike would cost around $6000. As of this writing, U.S. pricing hasn’t been revealed. However, in Canada, the Sprint 440 will cost $8499 CAD, which is about $6100 at current exchange rates. That’s roughly $1000 more than a 2027 Royal Enfield Meteor 350, though it’s around what Triumph charges for its 400 models.

But, crucially, it’s almost $4000 less expensive than Harley’s current entry-level model, the 975cc Nightster. And while everything’s expensive these days, four grand still buys quite a bit of gasoline for riding. We’ll just have to wait until spring 2027 to see if the Sprint 440 hits the ground running.

#4376. 8 Elden Ring Details That Suggest Some of the Biggest Mysteries Still Aren’t Solved

Melissa Sarnowski is a Gaming Writer at DualShockers who has been covering games professionally since 2022. She specializes in lists, reviews, and features, with additional experience writing guides for Hardcore Gamer. Before joining DualShockers, Melissa contributed to Screen Rant, and she currently writes for CBR and

Elden Ring is weird, and I mean that in the best way. FromSoftware builds elaborate worlds in each game the developers make, and the effort and attention to detail that goes into those worlds mean that you can spend dozens of hours digging into the lore and still not have a clear idea of it.

Bored with the way you go about your journey in The Lands Between? Here are the 10 best ways to make your second Elden Ring playthrough different.

This design for lore also means that you likely won't find an answer to every question. If you're like me, then the mystery is part of the charm. It keeps you wondering, and that keeps you playing as you search for answers that might not fully exist in-game in as straightforward of a way as you’d wish.

My favorite mystery is the Gloam-Eyed Queen. You never get to see her, but multiple items refer to her, and you learn that she was the main rival of Marika. It's also heavily implied that she still has some followers in the Lands Between.

However, we don't know her real identity, what happened to her, or where she is if she's alive. One interesting theory is that Melina is the Gloam-Eyed Queen due to her one eye seeming sealed shut, but when it's open in the Frenzied Flame ending, it has a gloam color to it.

This is a bit interesting because we know why the Land of Shadow was separated from the Lands Between. Marika effectively sealed away her past in the Land of Shadow, but more importantly, she was able to block access to the exact gate that let her ascend to godhood. Of course, she would put measures in place that prevented others from getting power like that.

The mystery is how she separated it and how Miquella was able to create an entrance that others could follow him through. However, the methods aren't exactly important enough to impact the lore much, and we just don't know the extent of Marika’s abilities.

Aside from its name, there are multiple mentions of locations beyond the Lands Between. We also know that the Tarnished, when they had their Grace removed by Marika, were sent away and returned later. So, that means that the Lands Between is a place that can be accessed from other lands.

It also raises the question as to why the Lands Between is so unique and has the Erdtree and, previously, the Crucible. Are the other lands not worth the attention of the Outer Gods, or is it just that the gods we know of aren't interested, but others might be? There's just not enough information to find an answer.

The Greater Will is well-known, and a few gods like the God of Rot, Formless Mother, and Frenzied Flame are mentioned enough that we know they exist and have some interest in the Lands Between. However, we really don't know much about the gods or what they want from this land.

These Elden Ring bosses are underrated and deserve more praise.

It's obvious that the Erdtree is what they're after, but the Erdtree is almost certainly built on the Crucible, which could be another goal or the main goal. But the Greater Will apparently has the ability to create and defeat gods, so it seems strange that it would want power from the Lands Between unless it's to keep it out of the hands of other gods.

Nokstella alone is filled with so much mystery that it's difficult to condense into a summary when you need a ton of context and explanations. Honestly, you could write a novella on the many unanswered questions that come from this location.

The Nox, who built Nokstella after rebelling against the Greater Will unsuccessfully, were originally thought to be connected to the Numen and Marika, but the DLC puts Marika in a completely different location. But then you have the connections between the Black Knives and Marika, along with the Black Knives being connected to the Nox. There are too many threads and almost no answers here.

Placidusax has two heads when you encounter him for his boss fight, but he also has a few stumps where more heads once were. The story is that his missing heads were cut off by Bayle, and you can find that two of his heads are with Bayle when you see him in the Shadow of the Erdtree DLC.

Except that's not accounting for every head. Placidusax has two remaining. Bayle has two of the missing ones, but if you look at Placidusax’s model and the Old Lord's Talisman, it shows that he should have five heads. The problem is that we have no idea what happened to the fifth one.

There are seven walking mausoleums in Elden Ring, and we can assume that they were made by the Nox because of their design, which matches the buildings in Nokstella, a style found nowhere else. The interesting part is that we're told they house soulless demigods, so those in the same state as Godwyn.

If that's true, then the bodies in them must be Marika’s children. A ghost even tells you when talking about one that it has Marika's unwanted child in it. When you start Elden Ring, you feel like you know who Marika's children are, but the details of the world let you know that she apparently had far more children than you think as you dig into the lore.

I'm fascinated by the Gate of Divinity, and I think it's one of the most well-known mysteries if you played the DLC or even watched the trailer for it. This is where Marika ascended to godhood, and Miquella later followed in her footsteps, albeit with a much shorter reign since you end it immediately.

Yet we know nothing about this gate other than the fact that it grants divinity. There seem to be requirements for being able to use it successfully, but beyond that we don't know how or why it works. We don't even know where it connects to.

FromSoftware makes such fascinating games that leave you thinking about them even years after they were released, encouraging you to explore every bit of content. Unfortunately, like most of their games, we're probably not going to get answers for every mystery in Elden Ring.

FromSoftware games are full of many NPCs, but many of them are hurt by your intervention, and not helped. Here are the best/saddest examples.

The 2022 action RPG by From Software joins the Souls-like subgenre by presenting one of the most punishing games in the field with grotesque, memorable bosses to keep you up at night. Inside a world built by Hidetaka Miyazaki and Game of Thrones writer George R.R. Martin, Elden Ring's gothic landscape, unforgiving combat, and top-tier exploration will keep you invested well into the year.

#4373. Jeep Wrangler Scrambler SRT Concept Previews the Future by Pulling from the Past

Remember the CJ-8 Scrambler? This one is like that, but with an independent front suspension and a trophy truck–inspired rear axle.

CORRECTION 11/3/26: This story has been updated to correct details about the origins of the original CJ-8 Scrambler.

Long before the Jeep Gladiator pickup truck, the Scrambler from the 1980s was the brand’s first cargo-bed-toting model. Now, Jeep has plans to resurrect the Scrambler as a production vehicle, with a new SRT concept revealed at this year’s SEMA show providing a preview.

Unlike the original CJ-8 Scrambler, which was based on a stretched CJ-7 chassis, the new Scrambler SRT concept is built on a Wrangler foundation. For the bits under the bodywork, Jeep worked with a Dakar-winning off-road driver to develop the Scrambler SRT’s suspension, which, for the first time on a Wrangler-branded vehicle, has an independent front setup. The high-travel front suspension pairs with a trophy truck–inspired rear axle, which builds on the design Jeep first showcased on the race-winning Gladiator Striker.

See all results for new 2028 Jeep Wrangler Scrambler for sale near 94043

The new Scrambler’s front end is instantly recognizable as a Jeep, though it looks a bit different from the rest of the brand’s lineup. For starters, the grille takes on a slightly retro style and sports a bit of an overbite. Then there’s the prominent hood scoop atop the engine cover and oversized fender flares, both of which are fitting for a truck wearing SRT badges. The concept is finished in a suitably loud Punk’n orange paint that gives Toyota’s Solar Octane paint a run for its money.

The goal with the Scrambler SRT, according to Tim Kuniskis, who now fills the role of head of American Brands, SRT Performance and Direct Connection, Stellantis North America, was to find out what happens when “SRT stops treating the trail as the limit and builds the ultimate open-air desert weapon.”

To that end, Jeep decided that the Scrambler SRT concept needed a V-8 under the hood. Unfortunately, we don’t know exactly which V-8 the truck is equipped with. Given the SRT badges on the sides, though, we think it’s a safe bet that the concept is rocking either the supercharged 6.2-liter Hellcat engine or the 6.4-liter Hemi 392. Either engine would provide suitable performance, but, knowing Kuniskis, the Hellcat is the likelier choice.

The Scrambler SRT concept is the first public appearance of the Scrambler name since Jeep confirmed plans for the model to return at its investor relations day back in May. When it does arrive, there will likely be a full lineup of Scramblers, with an SRT version sitting at the top of the line. The official timeline is still up in the air, as are official style and mechanical details, but the Scrambler SRT concept gives us a great preview of future production models, which we think could arrive in 2028.

Battlefield 6 has pushed back its next season by nearly a month in order to refine Season 2 content and implement more of players' feedback.

Battlefield Studios has released its first official communication in 2026. Rather than unveil the second season of Battlefield 6, however, the developer instead announced a delay. The currently ongoing Season 1 was initially meant to end on Tuesday, January 20, hence why the developer had to communicate something this week.

Season 1 will now end on Tuesday, February 17, which is also when Season 2 will kick off. Given the current sentiment around the game, this news isn’t surprising in the least.

In the blog post announcing the delay, BF Studios said that the decision to extend the current season and push back the start of the next one allows for extra time to “further polish and refine” Season 2 content.

The developer did not offer any hints about Season 2, but there’s an incredibly brief teaser trailer featuring a soldier wearing a gas mask emerging from an environment drenched in toxic gas.

Given that Battlefield 6’s battle royale mode Redsec does not utilise the popular encroaching gas mechanic (using an encroaching ring of fire instead), it’s possible that we may be looking at something new in multiplayer akin to Battlefield 1. Of course, this may just be a visual piece that doesn’t reflect the gameplay of Season 2.

Escalating the fight with new threats on the battlefield.Season 2 begins February 17. pic.twitter.com/fGMegJJuTj

What we are getting news of today, however, is the game’s next patch. This extension update is going to arrive next week, on January 20, when Season 1 was supposed to end. It’s bringing new weekly challenges to the game, but its biggest addition is yet another Bonus Path to the battle pass. You can also expect the free daily login rewards to continue, alongside other periods of double XP.

Similar to other Bonus Paths, the new Frostfire Bonus Path can be completed alongside the Season 1 battle pass. You’ll need 110 Bonus Path Points in total if you want to earn everything it has to offer, with each tier requiring 10 points. It is worth noting, however, that Frostfire Points are only earned through weekly challenges, meaning there won’t be any bonus challenges associated with it.

Frostfire includes several new customisation rewards, of course, such as a Weapon Package, soldier skin, XP boosts and the usual run of unlocks.

Though the latest blog post may be devoid of any real details on Season 2, BF Studios confirmed that Battlefield Labs will play a larger role in offering a preview of what’s to come, so it’s entirely possible that the testing initiative will soon open its doors to players with an early look at some of the maps and other content planned for Season 2.
